title: Everything in One Place
tagline: One login. Every tool. Shared context.
heroAlt: Everything in one place — unified business platform

section1.heading: The SaaS tax
section1.body1: The average small business uses 8 to 12 software tools. Each with its own login, data model, billing cycle, and learning curve. None of them talk to each other natively. The business owner becomes the integration layer — manually copying data between apps and paying a third tool to make two others pretend to cooperate.
section1.body2: The subscription cost isn't even the real tax. It's the cognitive tax. The context switching. The "which tool has the latest version?" question. The onboarding tax when every new hire needs 10 accounts. The Zapier workflow that breaks silently on a Saturday.

section2.heading: One voice note, six updates
section2.quote: "Henderson kitchen remodel is done. Took 4 hours, used the remaining tile from inventory. Client was happy — wants a quote for the bathroom next."
section2.intro: From that single voice note, VOIS updates:
updates: Time tracking → 4 hours logged and closed
Invoice → draft generated from project scope
CRM timeline → updated with completion + new interest
New opportunity → bathroom quote added to pipeline
section2.outro: Six "modules" updated from one input — because they share the same database, not six APIs stitched together with hope.
